items.markdown: **Alessio Benavoli** received the MS (2004) and PhD (2008) degrees in Computer and Control Engineering from the University of Firenze, Italy. From April 2007 to May 2008, he worked for SELEX-Sistemi Integrati, Rome, Italy as system analyst. He has collaborated with the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering at the University of Melbourne, Australia and with the SYSTeMS Group at Ghent University, Belgium. Currently, he is working as post-doc researcher at IDSIA in Lugano, Switzerland. His research interests are in the areas of imprecise probabilities, decision-making under uncertainty, constrained estimation, filtering, control, multiple-sensor multiple-target tracking and optimal communication strategies in sensor networks.

items.markdown: **Marco Zaffalon** Marco Zaffalon (Graduate in Computer Science, 1991; PhD in Applied Mathematics, 1998) is a Professor at IDSIA (http://www.idsia.ch), in Switzerland, where he leads a research group in imprecise probability. He is Area Editor for imprecise probability of the International Journal of Approximate Reasoning. Formerly, he was Founding Member, Secretary, and later President of the Society for Imprecise Probability: Theories and Applications (http://www.sipta.org). He co-chaired the conferences ISIPTA ’03 and ISIPTA ’07. His research interests are in Bayesian and credal networks, credal classification, incomplete information and missing data, coherent lower previsions and the foundations of imprecise probability.

items.markdown: **Enrique Miranda** (Graduate in Mathematics, 1999; PhD in Mathematics and Statistics, 2003) is currently a Professor at the Department of Statistics and Operations Research at the University of Oviedo (Spain). He previously worked as an Associate Professor at Rey Juan Carlos University in Madrid (Spain). He is currently in the editorial board of the International Journal of Approximate Reasoning and of the Journal on Uncertain Systems, and holds also the position of Treasurer at the Executive Committee of the Society for Imprecise Probability: Theories and Applications (SIPTA). He has collaborated with the SYSTeMS Group at Ghent University (Belgium), the IDSIA Institute in Lugano (Switzerland) and with the Beijing University of Technology (China). His research interests are the modelisation of uncertainty and imprecision, and has worked on models of coherent lower previsions, random sets, possibility measures and belief functions, among others.
